claim: The paper presents a broad overview of LLM research, including architecture, training, fine-tuning, multimodal models, evaluation, applications, and challenges.
evidence: This article provides an overview of the literature on a broad range of LLM-related concepts. ... This review article is intended to provide not only a systematic survey but also a quick, comprehensive reference for the researchers and practitioners...
label: supported

claim: Transformers, increased computational capabilities, and large-scale training data contributed to breakthroughs in language models.
evidence: Recently, significant breakthroughs have been witnessed in language models, primarily attributed to transformers [1], increased computational capabilities, and the availability of large-scale training data.
label: supported

claim: GPT-3 demonstrated zero-shot transfer to downstream tasks without fine-tuning.
evidence: The early work on LLMs, such as T5 [10] and mT5 [11] employed transfer learning until GPT-3 [6] showed LLMs are zero-shot transferable to downstream tasks without fine-tuning.
label: supported

claim: The paper says LLMs have no running-cost or hardware requirements.
evidence: The LLMs abilities to solve diverse tasks with human-level performance come at the cost of slow training and inference, extensive hardware requirements, and higher running costs.
label: contradicted

claim: The paper identifies tokenization as a preprocessing step in LLM training.
evidence: Tokenization [59] is an essential pre-processing step in LLM training that parses the text into non-decomposing units called tokens.
label: supported

claim: The paper lists WordPiece, byte pair encoding (BPE), and unigram language modeling among commonly used tokenization schemes.
evidence: Some of the commonly used tokenization schemes in LLMs include wordpiece [62], byte pair encoding (BPE) [61], and unigramLM [60].
label: supported

claim: The paper states that standard self-attention has O(n) time complexity.
evidence: Self-attention has O(n2) time complexity which becomes infeasible for large sequences.
label: contradicted

claim: Flash Attention uses input tiling to reduce memory reads and writes between GPU high-bandwidth memory and on-chip SRAM.
evidence: To speed up, flash attention employs input tiling to minimize the memory reads and writes between the GPU high bandwidth memory (HBM) and the on-chip SRAM.
label: supported

claim: The paper describes data parallelism as replicating the model across devices and dividing batch data among them.
evidence: Data parallelism replicates the model on multiple devices where data in a batch gets divided across devices. At the end of each training iteration weights are synchronized across devices.
label: supported

claim: The paper says deduplication can be performed at sentence, document, and dataset levels.
evidence: This can be performed at multiple levels, like sentences, documents, and datasets.
label: supported

claim: The paper describes a causal decoder as using an encoder to process the input before generating output.
evidence: Causal Decoder: A type of architecture that does not have an encoder and processes and generates output using a decoder, where the predicted token depends only on the previous time steps.
label: contradicted

claim: The paper defines mixture-of-experts as using independent experts and a router to route tokens to experts.
evidence: Mixture-of-Experts: It is a variant of transformer architecture with parallel independent experts and a router to route tokens to experts.
label: supported

claim: The paper says scaling laws relate model parameters, dataset size, and computational resources to model performance.
evidence: Scaling laws study the optimal combination of model parameters, dataset size, and computational resources that predict the improvement in the model performance.
label: supported

claim: Instruction-tuning uses instruction-formatted data containing instructions and input-output pairs.
evidence: The pre-trained model is fine-tuned on instruction formatted data i.e., instruction and an input-output pair.
label: supported

claim: The paper states that alignment-tuning is intended to make models helpful, honest, and harmless.
evidence: It ensures LLMs operate according to human intentions and values. A model is defined to be an “aligned” model if the model fulfills three criteria of helpful, honest, and harmless or “HHH” [99].
label: supported

claim: The paper says self-consistency improves chain-of-thought performance by generating multiple responses and selecting the most frequent answer.
evidence: Self-Consistency: Improves CoT performance by generating multiple responses and selecting the most frequent answer [104].
label: supported

claim: The paper reports that Codex generates only one program version for each description.
evidence: Similarly, Codex generates 100 versions of a program by repetitive sampling for a given description, which produces a working solution for 77.5% of the problems passing unit tests.
label: contradicted

claim: The paper reports the exact number of GPUs used to train GPT-3.
evidence: The GPT-3 architecture is the same as the GPT-2 [5] but with dense and sparse attention in transformer layers similar to the Sparse Transformer [67]. It shows that large models can train on larger batch sizes with a lower learning rate...
label: insufficient_evidence

claim: The paper states that LLaMA-2 was trained with 40% more data than LLaMA-1 and uses a larger context length and grouped-query attention.
evidence: The pre-trained model has 40% more training data with a larger context length and grouped-query attention.
label: supported

claim: The paper claims that all LLMs are trained exclusively on English data.
evidence: mT5 [11]: A multilingual T5 model [10] trained on the mC4 dataset with 101 languages. ... The model uses a larger vocabulary size of 250,000 to cover multiple languages.
label: contradicted
